newsitem.title: USA: Three oil tankers stalled by Valdez port probe.
newsitem.headline: Three oil tankers stalled by Valdez port probe.

text.p: Three oil tankers stayed docked at Alaska's Valdez port Tuesday as pipeline officials investigated a likely link between an oil slick and the port's ballast-water-treatment plant, a port official said.
"There's one (ship) in anchorage and three at the piers," said Joe McGuiness, a U.S. Coast Guard operations officer.
The docked ships are Overseas Washington at 91,697 dead-weight-tonnes, Overseas Juno at 122,409 dead-weight-tonnes,and Arco Alaska at 191,460 dead-weight-tonnes, he said.
Another ship, operated by Sea River, was in anchorage, but its weight was unknown, according to officials.
The investigation has not caused a backup of ships but has forced tankers to depart Valdez with crude loads about 20 percent to 30 percent lower than normal, state and Coast Guard officials said.
State and federal laws mandate tankers must retain their loads of oily ballast water, which balances empty ships during their journey to Alaska.
A malfunction in the trans-Alaska pipeline's treatment plant probably caused a patchy sheen that appeared Friday in Valdez, a state official said earlier Tuesday.
"We don't understand how long the plant is going to be affected," McGuiness said.
